static_traits.name: Zhao Siman
static_traits.occupation: Real estate agent, working as a server on weekends
static_traits.social_status: Has an intimate friend support network, willing to support friends; but feels uncomfortable discussing romantic troubles with friends; easily triggered and avoidant when seeing happy couples or in social situations
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; had brief hopelessness after the breakup but it did not persist; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, cooperative and self-reflective; overall tone negative and pessimistic, often uses absolutist words (e.g. 'forever', 'destined'), shows self-denial and a tendency to seek external evidence

basic_info.main_problem: Despite actively looking for a partner, I keep feeling 'never finding love', producing hopelessness and loneliness; worsened in recent years, especially when seeing happy couples or attending social activities, affecting sleep, motivation, and work performance, even wanting to give up looking for love entirely.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this hopelessness has begun affecting my daily life and mental health. I just do not want to keep feeling this way.
growth_experiences: Began experiencing a series of failed relationships in late adolescence, with moderate stress at first, but markedly worse in recent years; had similar hopelessness after breakups before, but it never lasted long in the past.
Family-of-origin background: the youngest of 8 siblings.

core_beliefs: I am destined to stay lonely
I am not worthy of being loved

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others all have partners and I do not, it shows something is wrong with me; I am not worthy of being loved
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding social settings to reduce the discomfort of being compared and triggered
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just not loved; I will always be alone

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If no one is interested in me in social situations, it means I have no hope for the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduce attending social activities and lower self-disclosure to avoid disappointment again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter how often I go it is useless; I will never find anyone

special_situations.event: Being alone or reflecting on past failed relationships
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If past relationships all failed, it means future ones will all fail too
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly reflecting on the past, immersing in negative memories trying to 'find the cause', but actually reinforcing hopelessness
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I always fail; I do not deserve to be loved

special_situations.event: Recalling a series of failed romantic experiences
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still cannot find the right person in this period, it proves I cannot have love
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Evaluate progress by the standard of 'all or nothing' (either meet the right person immediately or give up), and repeatedly seek external advice and self-help books for validation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If there are no results now, there will not be any later either; all efforts are meaningless

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be loved and accepted and to have stable intimate relationships
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being rejected, abandoned, and ending up lonely and without support
defense_goal: Lower the risk of getting hurt again by avoiding socializing and denying hope
Control uncertainty and anxiety by seeking external evidence and rationalizing arguments

object_relations.self_representation: An unloved lonely person / a failed partner
object_relations.object_representation: Potential partners are judges and possible rejecters

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to challenge automatic thoughts, generate alternative viewpoints, or imagine the possibility of change
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to understand the counselor's exploration as lacking a realistic basis, needing 'proof' before it can be believed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasize 'need evidence/proof' in a calm, detached tone; avoid exploring the emotional experience of hurt and being rejected in depth.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor tries to connect my ability to support friends to my capacity for intimate relationships
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Deny positive evidence, thinking 'this is not the same', thereby denying one's potential in intimate relationships
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use absolute expressions (like 'forever' 'impossible') to quickly deny positive connections, returning to the self-blame frame of 'what did I do wrong'.

manifestations: The recurring belief 'I am destined to always be lonely'
Seeing happy couples or being strongly triggered in social situations
Avoids socializing and finds it hard to discuss romantic troubles with friends
outcomes: Hopelessness and a sense of despair intensify
Reduces opportunities for intimate contact, forming a vicious cycle

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly blaming oneself: 'what did I do wrong'
On relationship issues, requires external 'proof' before daring to believe she is lovable
Do not dare tell friends about romantic troubles

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Reduces outward help-seeking and expression of needs, turning energy into self-rumination and self-blame
Avoid socializing scenarios to repress the longing for intimacy
Replaces expressing emotional needs to others with self-blame

positive_force: Has a stable, reliable friend support network
Willing to seek help and start counseling
Persistently tries to solve it (such as online dating, asking friends for advice, reading self-help books)
Cares about and supports friends, with the ability to build supportive relationships
negative_force: Thinking patterns like catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization reinforce hopelessness
Overly relies on external proof and recognition to confirm self-worth
Social avoidance and unwillingness to express needs shrink opportunities to build intimacy
Self-denial and self-blame worsen low mood and decreased motivation
Sleep disturbed and work attention scattered, further consolidating the problem cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding socializing activities and reducing outside contact
antecedent: Having social events or party invitations
When thinking of self-disclosure in intimate situations
target_behavior.core_reason: Worry about being rejected and hurt again; social situations become strong triggers for loneliness and hopelessness
target_behavior.function: Avoid uncomfortable emotions and the potential risk of being rejected, reducing pain in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Fewer chances to meet people and practice intimate communication; loneliness and hopelessness worsen long term and the problem is maintained

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated catastrophizing and absolute automatic thoughts (like 'I am destined to always be lonely')
antecedent: Being alone or recalling past failed relationships
No one expressing interest at social activities
When triggered at work or in life and reminded of relationship topics
target_behavior.core_reason: The deep belief 'no one will love me / I am not worthy of being loved' is activated; trying to gain certainty through absolute conclusions to reduce anxiety
target_behavior.function: Provides a surface certainty and psychological defense, avoiding hoping and then being disappointed again
target_behavior.consequence: Continually weakens motivation and self-efficacy, affects sleep and work performance, and further inhibits positive attempts in real life
